principles: Start from required outcomes and artifacts, decompose them into information objects, then synthesize interaction and process flow from those information needs.
Model information movement before process-graph synthesis. The Ordo process graph is a projection of the validated authoring information model, not the primary design source.
Use one typed information-flow topology for scalar values, structured records, evidence, documents, reports, manifests, packages and intermediate artifacts.

Every information object has a stable catalog definition and a runtime value instance. Value state and validation state are independent: unknown or not_applicable can still be explicitly validated or approved when business semantics allow it.
Supported value states include unset, value, unknown and not_applicable. Supported validation lifecycle includes draft, validated, approved and stale.
Any post-validation mutation that affects validated information makes its validation evidence stale and invalidates dependent evidence until the relevant deterministic gate reruns.
Group information objects into semantic bundles to support progressive intake, proposal-first interaction, shared validation and coherent analyst review.

Prefer progressive intake: use an initial free description to seed multiple information objects, derive or propose downstream values from approved information, and ask the human only for unresolved business authority or semantic trade-offs.
Reject irrelevant or structurally invalid information before it contaminates durable state when deterministic checks can decide this.
Artifacts are first-class information-flow nodes and may be intermediate or terminal. Artifact materialization and verification must be represented in the same topology.
Use typed edges such as provided_by, derived_from, validated_by, approved_by, consumed_by, materializes, invalidates, packages and depends_on rather than an untyped diagram.
The authoring information model is internal Vibe implementation state and must project to ordinary canonical Ordo constructs; it must not extend Ordo syntax.

Bidirectional traceability is mandatory once process synthesis begins: every required authoring entity must be materially represented in Ordo, and every authoring-managed Ordo element must trace back to the authoring model.
Machine-detectable information-model or projection defects remain behind the analyst visibility barrier and must be repaired before a candidate is handed off.

Persist progressive interaction as an authoring projection that references information objects/groups; interaction order is derived from information needs and authority, not invented independently of the information model.
